identity.title: On the Generalization Capacities of MLLMs for Spatial Intelligence

problem.claim: The paper studies how MLLMs processing RGB inputs for spatial tasks such as 3D localization and navigation generalize across cameras.

gap.claim: The authors argue that RGB-only approaches ignore camera parameters, entangle object properties with viewpoint, and therefore overfit training-camera distributions instead of learning generalizable 3D geometry.

contributions.claim: Proposes a Camera-Aware MLLM framework for spatial MLLMs.
Combines per-visual-token camera-intrinsics embeddings, camera-parameter-varying augmentation, and distillation of geometric priors from a 3D vision foundation model.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present camera awareness as a framework-level approach that explicitly conditions spatial reasoning on camera intrinsics, augments camera variation, and transfers 3D geometric priors.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that camera-aware MLLMs substantially outperform naive counterparts, especially on cross-camera generalization tests for spatially grounded tasks.
The authors interpret these results as indicating that camera awareness is beneficial and a prerequisite for robust, generalizable spatial intelligence in MLLMs.

narrative_sequence.summary: RGB-based MLLMs show potential for 3D localization and navigation.

The authors argue RGB-only models cannot reliably generalize across cameras because omitted camera parameters create an irresolvable viewpoint–object ambiguity and encourage training-camera overfitting.
They propose Camera-Aware MLLM, using camera-conditioned visual tokens, synthetic camera variation, and distilled 3D geometric priors.
The abstract reports substantial gains over naive counterparts, particularly in cross-camera tests.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links a specific failure mode—camera/object entanglement—to three design choices targeting conditioning, data variation, and geometric priors.

lessons.interpretation: A strong method narrative can align each architectural component with a diagnosed source of non-generalization.
lessons.application: When presenting a robustness method, map each intervention explicitly to the mechanism believed to cause the target failure.
lessons.exception: This mapping is unsuitable when the proposed components are exploratory or their causal roles are not separately motivated.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify datasets, camera ranges, baselines, metrics, or numerical effect sizes.
It does not report ablations separating the contributions of the three framework components.
The claimed prerequisite status is an author interpretation, not independently verified here.
